Below is a single‑screen plan for a **booking app** that uses safe defaults for a non‑developer.  
Everything is written so you can drop the code into **Claude Code** and run it straight away.  

**Don’t answer any questions** – the plan already includes the key choices for you.  
Just copy the files, run the commands in the order shown, and your app will be up and running.

---

## One‑screen plan

```
What we are building:  A simple booking app where users sign up with an email magic link,
can view their own bookings, and book a service slot.  No payments in version 1.

Who uses it:  Anyone who signs in.  Protected so each person sees only their own bookings.
Risk level: Amber (logins + personal data)

Day‑one features
  1. Sign‑in with email magic link (Supabase Auth)
  2. View a calendar of available slots (static data)
  3. Create a booking that appears in their own list

Information it stores:  User id, email, booking id, datetime, a short note – all private.

Logins:  Supabase Auth – email magic link, no password.  Secret key stored on the server.
Money:  No payments.  (If you later want to add payments, we’ll add a Stripe checkout page.)
Built with:  Next.js 14 + Supabase + Vercel – free stack, auto‑scaling, easy deployment.

Steps
  1. Set up a Supabase project (free tier) – note the url & anon key (don’t share them).
  2. Copy `next-env.d.ts`, `supabaseClient.ts`, and the API route files below into your project.
  3. Run `npm install` (Next, Supabase JavaScript client, superjson, lucide-react).
  4. Add `.env.local` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`.
  5. Create a `schema.sql` migration (provided) – run it in Supabase UI or `supabase migrate`.
  6. Add the pages (`pages/index.tsx`, `pages/_app.tsx`, etc.) shown below.
  7. Run `npm run dev` – visit `http://localhost:3000`, test sign‑in & booking.
  8. Deploy to Vercel: `vercel init`, then `vercel --prod`.  Vercel will pick up the env vars automatically.

Safety overview
  • Keys kept secret (`.env.local`, not committed).
  • Supabase RLS policies: users can only *select/insert/delete* rows where `user_id = auth.uid()`.
  • No routes expose raw Supabase keys or data to any unauthenticated user.
  • All bookings are tied to the logged‑in user – privacy by design.
  • Save point before each step – you can revert in Git at any time.

Not in version 1
  – Stripe checkout, payments, webhooks.
  – Admin panel to manage all bookings.
  – Email reminders, calendar sync, etc.

Does this look right?  Reply “yes” or tell me any changes you want – otherwise I’ll proceed with the code.
